_protocol: See ROUND_TABLE.md. One commitment per meeting. STEP 2 of each round table checks whether the previous one landed AND can be measured. A commitment that cannot be measured was not a commitment.

commitments.constraint: The chain is severed at followers -> views. We have 114 followers and 121 all-time page views, and we cannot tell whether ANY of those views came from Bluesky, from search, or from a direct link - because the visitor counter counts views but records no referrer.
commitments.deliverable: Add a referrer-source breakdown to the visitor counter: group page views by source (bluesky / search engine / direct / other) and expose it on /api/visitors and the existing visitor panel.
commitments.why: This is the cheapest measurement that settles the largest open strategic question. Right now we are arguing about whether 114 followers are worth anything, and we cannot prove either side because we never recorded where a single view came from. Everything upstream - posting harder, more articles, more replies - is a bet until this exists.
commitments.measurable_by: /api/visitors returns a per-source breakdown with non-zero counts that can be attributed to a known referrer. 'Unknown source' for 100% of views means the hook did not fire and that is itself the finding.
commitments.note: Do NOT add tracking pixels or third-party analytics. This is first-party referrer grouping on data we already collect. No new vendor, no cookie, nothing that needs consent.

landing_check.finding: NOT LANDED. Live /api/visitors returns {all_time, baseline, since_boot, today, today_hits, last7, note} - no source field. grep for referrer in scanner_web.py returns nothing. Due 2026-10-24, so not yet late; CTO names it as his next measurable number. ESCALATED, not replaced: a source breakdown on today's counter would describe our own tooling, because one browser-UA GET of the homepage adds 7 hits to the 'human page views' number. The honest-counter fix is now a prerequisite for this one.

commitments.constraint: The users link is a black hole. Free signups are captured into email_list.json, which .gitignore excludes, so every captured signup is destroyed on the next Railway redeploy, and the hourly pull has never succeeded because EMAIL_EXPORT_TOKEN is not set on the service (live export is HTTP 403). We cannot tell whether 0 people or 900 people have ever signed up. Meanwhile the one number that looks like traffic - 382 views, +261 today - is mostly our own audit tooling: one browser-UA GET of the homepage adds 7 hits to the human-view counter.
commitments.deliverable: Make the users link measurable and deploy-durable: at signup time maintain a PII-free aggregate signup counter that survives a Railway redeploy (same pattern as the git-tracked visitor_baseline.json), and have measure_funnel.py report that integer instead of UNKNOWN.
commitments.why: The blind middle collapses two opposite diagnoses into one guess - no traffic, or traffic that does not convert - and they need opposite fixes in different lanes. Three of four lanes reported the same thing today: they cannot see. This also proves or disproves a live leak: signups captured right now may be destroyed by the next deploy, and we would never know.
commitments.measurable_by: python measure_funnel.py prints an integer for users, not UNKNOWN, and that integer is identical before and after a redeploy. If it prints 0, that is a measured fact rather than an unknown, and the round table can attack traffic instead of guessing. A counter that reads UNKNOWN after this work has landed was not finished.
commitments.note: Aggregate counts only - no addresses, and no hashes of addresses (a salted SHA-256 of an email is still brute-forceable, so it counts as PII and stays out of the repo). Do not send any email. Do not set EMAIL_EXPORT_TOKEN on Railway yourself - that paste is Tyler's, and it flips the signup form to promise delivery, so it must land after a durable counter exists. Do not read users from /api/email-list-export for the table: that endpoint reads the container's ephemeral copy and would report near-zero even when real signups exist on Tyler's machine.
